cases.name: a machine stays active and handles a later event

cases.name: a machine that reaches its state does not fail

cases.name: an unhandled rejection of an invoked promise fails the root

cases.name: an unhandled rejection of an invoked promise reaches the parent's error
cases.test: errors.test.ts > error handling > unhandled rejection of a promise actor should be reported to the existing error listener of its parent

cases.name: an unhandled rejection of a grandchild promise climbs to the root's error

cases.name: a failing initial assign fails the actor
cases.test: errors.test.ts > error handling > error thrown when resolving initial builtin entry action should error the actor immediately (the status after the start only: the snapshot before the start is not recorded, and a failed start records no snapshot, so the error does not show)

cases.name: a failing entry action of a transition's target fails the actor
cases.test: errors.test.ts > error handling > error thrown by a custom entry action when transitioning should error the actor (the status only: the vocabulary's failing assign stands for the custom action that throws, which a case cannot run, and a failed transition records no snapshot, so the error does not show)

cases.name: a guard that fails while transitioning fails the actor
cases.test: errors.test.ts > error handling > should error when a guard throws when transitioning (the status only: the vocabulary's failing guard stands for the guard that throws, and a failed transition records no snapshot, so the error does not show)

cases.name: an actor emits on every event and stays active
cases.test: errors.test.ts > error handling > actor continues to work normally after emit callback errors (the emitted events and the status only; the actor.on listener that throws is not ported)

excluded.test: errors.test.ts > error handling > does not cause an infinite loop when an error is thrown in subscribe
excluded.reason: asserts only how a subscriber that throws is treated (called once, its error reported globally); the format has no subscribe step, and the record holds neither a subscriber's calls nor the global error report. The machine's own part, an actor that reaches active and does not fail, is already the case 'a machine that reaches its state does not fail'. It would need a subscribe step with a subscriber that throws, and a record of a subscriber's calls and of the global error report

excluded.test: errors.test.ts > error handling > error thrown in initial custom entry action should error the actor
excluded.reason: needs a custom action that throws when it is executed, which is out of scope: custom actions are handed to on_action, not run as functions (doc: #differences-custom), so none can fail its actor. XState defers an initial custom action to start(), runs it there, fails the actor and still publishes the xstate.init snapshot, active, before the failed status. No built-in action stands for it, since XState's update() notes that no built-in deferred throws, and the vocabulary's failing assign throws while createActor resolves the initial state, before the start, which is the path of 'error thrown when resolving initial builtin entry action should error the actor immediately', ported as 'a failing initial assign fails the actor'

excluded.test: errors.test.ts > error handling > shouldn't execute deferred initial actions that come after an action that errors
excluded.reason: needs a custom action that throws when it is executed, which is out of scope: custom actions are handed to on_action, not run as functions (doc: #differences-custom). The test asserts that when an initial custom action throws at start(), XState clears the initial actions deferred after it, so the spy never runs; no built-in action throws in a deferred, and the vocabulary's failing assign throws while createActor resolves the initial state, so nothing after it is ever deferred and the spy's absence would hold whatever the deferral does
